pass_a_gloss: And if someone, as it were zealous for the greater gifts and counting happy rich witnesses and fathers who are witnesses who will beget hundredfold offspring and will take hundredfold lands and dwellings, seeks whether with reason those, beside the witnesses needy in life, will have the holding in things grasped by the mind multiplied, it must be said toward him that, as those who bore up under torments and toils displayed a brighter excellence in witness than those not examined in these, so those who, in addition to fondness for the body and fondness for living, cut through and broke apart the so many bonds of the world too, having employed the great charity toward God and having truly received the living reason of God, working and more cutting beyond every double-mouthed blade, have been able, having cut through the so many bonds and having fitted out for themselves feathers like an eagle, to turn back into the dwelling of the one presiding over them. It is fitting therefore, as for those not examined in torments and toils to give way in first rank toward those who showed endurance in joint-breaking devices and varied twisting machines and fire, thus also for us the needy, even if we bear witness, the reasoning suggests to step out from first rank for you who, through the charity in Christ toward God, tread on the cheating repute that reaches down upon the many, and the so great holding, and the fondness toward offspring.
pass_b_english: But suppose someone, as if “eagerly seeking the greater gifts” (1 Corinthians 12:31) and calling blessed the rich martyrs and the martyrs who are fathers, who will beget children a hundredfold and receive fields and houses a hundredfold, asks whether it is reasonable that they, compared with martyrs who were poor in this life, will have their possession among intelligible realities multiplied. We must tell him this. Just as those who endured tortures and pains have shown a more brilliant virtue in martyrdom than those not tested in these things, so too with those who, besides the love of the body and the love of life, have also cut through and burst so many worldly bonds. They have used a great love toward God and have truly taken up the living word of God, which is active and sharper “than any two-edged sword” (Hebrews 4:12); and having cut through so many bonds and made themselves wings like an eagle, they have been able to return “to the house” of “the one set over” them (Proverbs 23:5).

It is right, then, that just as those not tested in tortures and pains should yield the first place to those who showed their endurance on racks that wrench the joints, on twisting engines of every kind, and in fire, so also for us who are poor, even if we bear witness, reason prompts us to stand aside from the first place for you, who for the sake of love toward God in Christ trample on the deceitful glory that lays hold of the many, on such great possessions, and on affection for your children.

choices.choice: 2026-11-11: retranslated in full from Koetschau (GCS 2, ch. 15); the old English was a digest. The old English kept the order but rendered ὡσπερεί as 'harshly', made the deceitful glory 'hunted by many', and blurred the comparison with those tortured on the rack.
ἀσπερεὶ read ὡσπερεί ('as if'); μάρτυgas read μάρτυρας; ληψφομένους read ληψομένους; βασάτοις read βασάνοις; πιρὶ read πυρί; ἐνεπιδειξαμένους (M; P and Delarue ἐπιδειξαμένους) 'showed'.
Koetschau prints Delarue's ἀετός ('eagle') for αὐτός in M and P; translated 'like an eagle'.
τῷ (M margin, Delarue) read: 'besides the love of the body and the love of life'.
'Racks that wrench the joints' and 'twisting engines of every kind'.

source_text: Ἐὰν δὲ τις ἀσπερεὶ ζηλῶν χαρίσματα τὰ μείζονα καὶ μακαρίζων πλουσίους μάρτυρας καὶ πατέρας μάρτυρας ἕκατονταπλασίονα" γεννήσοντας τέχνα καὶ ἑκατονταπλασίονας ἀγροὶς καὶ οἰκίας ληψφομένους ζητῇ, εἰ εὐλόγως ἐχεῖνοι παρὰ τοὺς ἐν βίῳ πένητας μάρτυgas πολυπλασιαζομένην ἕξουσι τὴν ἐν νοητοῖς κτῆσιν, λεκτέον πρὸς αὐτὸν ὅτι, ὥσπερ οἱ βασάνους καὶ πόνους ὑπομείν αντες τῶν μὴ ἐν τούτοις ἐξητασμένων λαμπροτέραν ἐπεδείξαντο τὴν ἐν τῷ μαρτυρίῳ ἀρετὴν, οὕτως οἱ πρὸς τῷ φιλοσωματεῖν καὶ φιλοζωεῖν καὶ τοὺς τοσούτους χοσμικοὺς δεσμοὺς διακόψαντες καὶ διαῤῥήξαντες μεγάλῃ) τῇ πρὸς τὸν ϑεὸν ἀγάπῃ χρησάμενοι καὶ ἀληϑῶς ἀνειληφότες τὸν ζῶντα τοῦ ϑεοῦ λόγο» καὶ ἐνεργῆ καὶ τομώτερον «ὑπὲρ πᾶσαν μάχαιραν δίστομον" δεδύνηνται τοὺς τοσούτους διακόψαντες δεσμοὺς καὶ κατασχευάσαντες ἑαυτοῖς πτέρυγας ὥσπερ ἀετὸς ἐπιστρέψαι »εἰς τὸν οἶχον τοῦ προεστηκότος". ἑαυτῶν. ἄξιον οὖν ὥσπερ τοῖς μὴ ἐξετασϑεῖσιν ἐν βασάτοις καὶ πόνοις παραχωρεῖν πρωτείων πρὸς τοὺς ἐν ἀρϑρεμβόλοις καὶ ποιχίλοις στρεβλωτηρίοις καὶ πιρὶ ἐνεπιδειξαμένους τὴν ὑπομονὴν, οὕτως καὶ ἡμῖν τοῖς πένησι, κἂν μαρτυρήσωμεν, ὁ λόγος ὑποβάλλει ἐξίστασϑαι πρωτείων ὑμῖν τοῖς διὰ τὴν ἐν Χριστῷ πρὸς ϑεὸν ἀγάπην πατοῦσι τὴν ἀπατηλὴν δόξαν καὶ τῶν πολλῶν καϑικχνουμένην καὶ τὴν τοσαύτην κτῆσιν καὶ τὴν πρὸς τέχνα φιλοστοργίαν».
